

# Hypotheses
H1. People will report trusting doctors more than artificial intelligence for all the medical decisions that we present to them.

H2. The difference in trust between doctors and artificial intelligence will vary based on the perceived amount of needed quantitative reasoning believed to be needed to make that medical decision. 

H3.a. The capability of a decision-maker to use quantitative reasoning will correlate with the perceived competence of the decision-maker.

H3.b. The capability of a decision-maker to use intuition will correlate with the perceived warmth of the decision-maker.

H4.a. The perceived warmth of the decision-maker will mediate the differences in trust between the artificial intelligence and the doctor.

H4.b. The perceived competence of the decision maker will mediate the differences in trust between the artificial intelligence and the doctor.

# Cleaning
```{r}
describe(Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2$Int_Quant_10)
```

## Removing Non-Viable Participants
### Removing Preview & Test Worker
```{r}

Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Clean <- Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2[-c(1,2,3,4), ]

```


### Removing People Who Did Not Consent
```{r}
Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Clean <- Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Clean %>%
  filter(Consent == 1)

```

# PreRegistered Analysis

1. Our primary analysis will be a paired samples t-test to compare trust in doctors and artificial intelligence along every dimension of medical decisions. We will also compare doctors and artificial intelligence using paired samples t-tests on the medical decision dimensions we will create.

12 - Paired Samples T-Tests - Base

a. Rec_Inj
b. Diag_Inj
c. Pres_Inj
d. Rec_Ment
e. Diag_Ment
f. Pres_Ment
g. Rec_AcuS
h. Diag_AcuS
i. Pres_AcuS
j. Rec_ChronS
k. Diag_ChronS
l. Pres_ChronS

Combined
n. Diagnostic
m. Prescriptive
o. Preventative
p. Physical Health
q. Mental Health
r. Bodily Injury
s. Acute Sickness
t. Chronic Stress

2. We will also conduct a linear mixed-effect model to investigate the overall trust difference in doctors and artificial intelligence for all medical decisions without the composites. Next, we will run this linear mixed-effects model using people’s perceptions of quantitative reasoning/intuition needed to make accurate medical decisions.



3. Additionally, we will run a linear mixed-effect model to determine whether the perceived warmth and competence of the decision-maker mediate the difference in trust between doctors and artificial intelligence.



4. Finally, we will correlate mind perception, the capability to use intuition, the capability to use quantitative reasoning, competence, and warmth.

## Combine Trust

### Doc
```{r}
Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Clean <- Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Clean %>%
  mutate(
    Trust.Diagnosis.Doc     = (Trust.Diag_Inj.Doc + Trust.Diag_Ment.Doc  + Trust.Diag_AcuS.Doc  + Trust.Diag_ChronS.Doc )/4,
    Trust.Prescription.Doc   = (Trust.Pres_Inj.Doc  + Trust.Pres_Ment.Doc  + Trust.Pres_AcuS.Doc + Trust.Pres_ChronS.Doc )/4,
    Trust.Preventative.Doc   = (Trust.Rec_Inj.Doc  + Trust.Rec_Ment.Doc  + Trust.Rec_AcuS.Doc  + Trust.Rec_ChronS.Doc )/4,
    Trust.PhysHealth.Doc     = (Trust.Diag_Inj.Doc  + Trust.Diag_AcuS.Doc  + Trust.Diag_ChronS.Doc  + Trust.Rec_Inj.Doc  + Trust.Rec_AcuS.Doc  + Trust.Rec_ChronS.Doc  + Trust.Pres_Inj.Doc  + Trust.Pres_AcuS.Doc  + Trust.Pres_ChronS.Doc )/9,
    Trust.MentHealth.Doc    = (Trust.Diag_Ment.Doc  + Trust.Rec_Ment.Doc  + Trust.Pres_Ment.Doc )/3,
    Trust.BodyInj.Doc        = (Trust.Diag_Inj.Doc  + Trust.Rec_Inj.Doc  + Trust.Pres_Inj.Doc )/3,
    Trust.AcuteSic.Doc       = (Trust.Diag_AcuS.Doc  + Trust.Rec_AcuS.Doc  + Trust.Pres_AcuS.Doc )/3,
    Trust.ChronSic.Doc       = (Trust.Diag_ChronS.Doc  + Trust.Rec_ChronS.Doc  + Trust.Pres_ChronS.Doc)/3
  )


```

### AI
```{r}
Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Clean <- Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Clean %>%
  mutate(
    Trust.Diagnosis.AI     = (Trust.Diag_Inj.AI + Trust.Diag_Ment.AI  + Trust.Diag_AcuS.AI  + Trust.Diag_ChronS.AI )/4,
    Trust.Prescription.AI   = (Trust.Pres_Inj.AI  + Trust.Pres_Ment.AI  + Trust.Pres_AcuS.AI + Trust.Pres_ChronS.AI )/4,
    Trust.Preventative.AI   = (Trust.Rec_Inj.AI  + Trust.Rec_Ment.AI  + Trust.Rec_AcuS.AI  + Trust.Rec_ChronS.AI )/4,
    Trust.PhysHealth.AI     = (Trust.Diag_Inj.AI  + Trust.Diag_AcuS.AI  + Trust.Diag_ChronS.AI  + Trust.Rec_Inj.AI  + Trust.Rec_AcuS.AI  + Trust.Rec_ChronS.AI  + Trust.Pres_Inj.AI  + Trust.Pres_AcuS.AI  + Trust.Pres_ChronS.AI )/9,
    Trust.MentHealth.AI    = (Trust.Diag_Ment.AI  + Trust.Rec_Ment.AI  + Trust.Pres_Ment.AI )/3,
    Trust.BodyInj.AI        = (Trust.Diag_Inj.AI  + Trust.Rec_Inj.AI  + Trust.Pres_Inj.AI )/3,
    Trust.AcuteSic.AI       = (Trust.Diag_AcuS.AI  + Trust.Rec_AcuS.AI  + Trust.Pres_AcuS.AI )/3,
    Trust.ChronSic.AI       = (Trust.Diag_ChronS.AI  + Trust.Rec_ChronS.AI  + Trust.Pres_ChronS.AI)/3
  )


```



```{r}
Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Clean %>%
  dplyr::select(Trust.Diag_Inj.AI, Trust.Diag_AcuS.AI, Trust.Diag_ChronS.AI, Trust.Rec_Inj.AI, Trust.Rec_AcuS.AI, Trust.Rec_ChronS.AI, Trust.Pres_Inj.AI, Trust.Pres_AcuS.AI, Trust.Pres_ChronS.AI, Trust.Diag_Ment.AI, Trust.Rec_Ment.AI, Trust.Pres_Ment.AI) %>% describe()

```

## Creating Long Format Data

There are two types of long format data I want to analyse.

1. Qualities of the decision makers
2. Qualities of the decision.

The data then needs to be put into a long format with the data being double nested, first by decision, next by decision maker. Both of which are nested within participant. This will mean that the qualties of the decisions should be doubled, the qualties of the decision makers needs to repeat 12 times, and the trust in the decision should have distinct non-repearting values. This should look like:

ResponseID, Decision-Maker, Decision, Trust, Int_Quant, Quality_Of_DecisionMaker

This should mean I need to pivot the data 3 seperate times and remerge it. 


### Reducing Data Frame
```{r}

Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Tight_Variables <- c(

  "Trust.Diag_AcuS.AI", "Trust.Diag_ChronS.AI", "Trust.Diag_Inj.AI", "Trust.Diag_Ment.AI", "Trust.Pres_AcuS.AI", "Trust.Pres_ChronS.AI", "Trust.Pres_Inj.AI", "Trust.Pres_Ment.AI", "Trust.Rec_AcuS.AI", "Trust.Rec_ChronS.AI", "Trust.Rec_Inj.AI", "Trust.Rec_Ment.AI",
```

### Pivoting Longer
#### Decision Only


```{r}

Pivot_Ch1_St2_Decision <- Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Tight %>%
  dplyr::select('ResponseId', "ID", "Int_Quant.Diag_AcuS", "Int_Quant.Diag_ChronS", "Int_Quant.Diag_Inj", "Int_Quant.Diag_Ment" , "Int_Quant.Pres_AcuS", "Int_Quant.Pres_ChronS", "Int_Quant.Pres_Inj", "Int_Quant.Pres_Ment",  "Int_Quant.Rec_AcuS", "Int_Quant.Rec_ChronS", "Int_Quant.Rec_Inj", "Int_Quant.Rec_Ment") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Int_Quant"),
    names_to = c('Decision'),
    names_prefix = ("Int_Quant."),
    values_to = "Int_Quant"
  )
```

#### Trust Only
```{r}

Pivot_Ch1_St2_Trust <- Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Tight %>%
  dplyr::select('ResponseId',  "ID", "Trust.Diag_AcuS.AI", "Trust.Diag_AcuS.Doc", "Trust.Diag_ChronS.AI",  "Trust.Diag_ChronS.Doc", "Trust.Diag_Inj.AI", "Trust.Diag_Inj.Doc", "Trust.Diag_Ment.AI", "Trust.Diag_Ment.Doc", "Trust.Pres_AcuS.AI", "Trust.Pres_AcuS.Doc", "Trust.Pres_ChronS.AI", "Trust.Pres_ChronS.Doc", "Trust.Pres_Inj.AI", "Trust.Pres_Inj.Doc", "Trust.Pres_Ment.AI", "Trust.Pres_Ment.Doc", "Trust.Rec_AcuS.AI", "Trust.Rec_AcuS.Doc", "Trust.Rec_ChronS.AI", "Trust.Rec_ChronS.Doc", "Trust.Rec_Inj.AI", "Trust.Rec_Inj.Doc", "Trust.Rec_Ment.AI","Trust.Rec_Ment.Doc" ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Trust"),
    names_to = c('Remove_Later','Decision', "Decision_Maker" ),
        names_sep = "\\.",
    values_to = "Trust"
  )

```

### Linear Mixed Effects Modeling

Decision Maker can either be it's own nested value or just a covariate. The problem is that Decision_maker covaries with all these other covariates making them less effective. Not in a bad way but just something to think about.
```{r}

## *  Exp_AI_Medical + Decision_Maker * Exp_ME_General
HealthAlgorithm_O2_LMER_1 <-
  Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Long %>%
  lmer(Intuition ~ Decision_Maker + (1 + Decision_Maker|ResponseId), data = .)

summary(HealthAlgorithm_O2_LMER_1)
```

```{r}
tab_model(HealthAlgorithm_O2_LMER_1, show.std = TRUE)
```


The model with the interaction between decision maker and int_quant random effect makes this model explain 85% of the variance which is wild. Something to think about.
Addendum - This change is because I used Decision_Maker as a random effect. Though the interaction does improve by 3% with the interaction. Very interesting indeed.
+ Intuition + Quant 
```{r}
HealthAlgorithm_O2_LMER_1 <- lmer(Trust ~  Age + IsMale + Int_Quant +Intuition + Quant +  Warmth + Competence + Age*Decision_Maker + (1 + Int_Quant|ResponseId), data = Health_Algorithm_Objectivity_2_Long)

summary(HealthAlgorithm_O2_LMER_1)
```

## MPLus Automation

### Intuition
#### C
```{r}
Mediation_Intuition_C <- mplusObject(
  TITLE = "INTUITION MEDIATION C",

VARIABLE = "
USEVARIABLES ARE ID Trust IsDoc;

CLUSTER IS ID;",

ANALYSIS =  "TYPE IS TWOLEVEL RANDOM;",

MODEL =  
  "%WITHIN%
	Trust IsDoc;
	Trust ON IsDoc;
	%BETWEEN%
	Trust IsDoc;
	Trust ON IsDoc;
	IsDoc@0;",

OUTPUT = "SAMPSTAT STANDARDIZED(CLUSTER) STDYX TECH1 TECH8 CINTERVAL;",

usevariables = colnames(MPLus_HAO2_Long),

rdata = MPLus_HAO2_Long)


Mediation_Intuition_Output_C <-   mplusModeler(Mediation_Intuition_C, dataout = "Intuition_R_C.dat", modelout = "Intuition_R_C.inp", check = TRUE, run = TRUE, hashfilename = FALSE)


Intuition_Output_Mplus <- readModels("Intuition_R_C.out")

Intuition_Output_Mplus$parameters

Intuition_Output_Mplus$data_summary
```

```{r}

CLUSTER IS ID;",
```
